title: New Discovery Could Explain What Gives Mars its Red Color
titleZh: 新发现或可解释火星为何呈现红色
credits: Bryan Lynn wrote this story for VOA Learning English, based on reports from

sentences.en: Scientists say they might have identified the mineral on Mars that is responsible for making the planet appear red.
sentences.zh: 科学家称，他们或许已经找到了火星上使这颗行星呈现红色的矿物。

sentences.en: New data collected on Mars through several methods suggests the substance, called ferrihydrite, is likely found in dust and rock material across wide areas of the planet.
sentences.zh: 通过多种方法在火星上收集到的新数据显示，这种被称为水铁矿的物质很可能广泛分布于这颗行星的尘埃和岩石物质中。

sentences.en: The team carrying out the research describes ferrihydrite as an “iron oxide mineral.”
sentences.zh: 开展这项研究的小组将水铁矿描述为一种'氧化铁矿物'。

sentences.en: The mineral appears reddish in color and can form in water-rich environments.
sentences.zh: 这种矿物呈微红色，可以在富含水的环境中形成。

sentences.en: The scientists said discovering large amounts of it on Mars adds to existing evidence that the planet might have held a large supply of liquid water in the past.
sentences.zh: 科学家表示，在火星上发现大量这种物质，进一步增加了火星过去可能拥有大量液态水的证据。

sentences.en: The research was carried out by an international team led by America’s Brown University and the University of Bern in Switzerland.
sentences.zh: 这项研究由美国布朗大学和瑞士伯尔尼大学领导的一个国际团队完成。

sentences.en: The findings recently appeared in a study published in Nature Communications.
sentences.zh: 这些发现最近发表在一本《自然·通讯》期刊的研究论文中。

sentences.en: The researchers noted that scientists have long wondered about the exact substance that gives Mars – which is also known as the Red Planet – its deep red color.
sentences.zh: 研究人员指出，科学家们长期以来一直对赋予火星——也被称为红色行星——深红色的确切物质感到好奇。

sentences.en: Past studies had suggested a mineral called hematite might be the cause.
sentences.zh: 过去的研究曾提出，一种名为赤铁的矿物可能是造成这一现象的原因。

sentences.en: The study is based on Martian data collected by several spacecraft.
sentences.zh: 这项研究基于多艘航天器在火星上收集到的数据。

sentences.en: These include the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, operated by the American space agency NASA.
sentences.zh: 其中包括由美国航天局NASA运营的火星侦察轨道器。

sentences.en: In addition, information was captured by instruments aboard the European Space Agency’s (ESA's) Mars Express and Trace Gas orbiters.
sentences.zh: 此外，信息还由欧洲航天局（ESA）的火星快车号和微量气体轨道器上的仪器捕捉到。

sentences.en: Some data also came from exploring vehicles, called rovers, operating on Mars.
sentences.zh: 部分数据还来自在火星上运行的、被称为漫游车的探测车辆。

sentences.en: In their examinations, the researchers also used manmade, or synthetic, material designed to look and feel similar to real Martian dust.
sentences.zh: 在考察中，研究人员还使用了人工合成的、外观和触感与真实火星尘埃相似的材料。

sentences.en: Adomas Valantinas currently works as a researcher at Brown University’s Department of Earth, Environment & Planetary Sciences.
sentences.zh: 阿多马斯·瓦兰提纳斯目前在布朗大学地球、环境与行星科学系担任研究员。

sentences.en: He helped write the study.
sentences.zh: 他参与了这项研究的撰写。

sentences.en: Valantinas noted the mystery of why Mars is red had been considered “for hundreds, if not thousands, of years.”
sentences.zh: 瓦兰提纳斯指出，火星为何呈红色的谜团'已被探讨数百年，甚至数千年'。

sentences.en: Valantinas recognized his team was not the first to consider ferrihydrite as a possible reason for the coloring of Mars.
sentences.zh: 瓦兰提纳斯承认，他的团队并非第一个将水铁矿视为火星着色可能原因的研究者。

sentences.en: But he noted, “it has never been proven as we have now, using observational data and novel laboratory methods…”
sentences.zh: 但他指出，'它从未被证明过，而我们现在通过观测数据和创新的实验室方法做到了……'

sentences.en: Valantinas noted the discovery of widespread ferrihydrite suggests Mars once held liquid water that would have made it possible for the planet to support some form of life.
sentences.zh: 瓦兰提纳斯指出，水铁矿广泛存在的发现表明，火星曾经拥有液态水，这可能使这颗行星得以支撑某种形式的生命。

sentences.en: "Our study reveals that ferrihydrite formation on Mars required the presence of both oxygen…and water capable of reacting with iron,” he added.
sentences.zh: "我们的研究表明，火星上水铁矿的形成需要氧气的存在……以及能与发生反应的水，"他补充道。

sentences.en: “These conditions were very different from the dry, cold environment of Mars today."
sentences.zh: "这些条件与今天火星干燥寒冷的环境大不相同。"

sentences.en: John Mustard is a planetary expert at Brown University and was a co-writer of the study.
sentences.zh: 约翰·马斯特德是布朗大学的行星问题专家，也是该研究的共同撰写者。

sentences.en: He called it “a door-opening opportunity” for future research.
sentences.zh: 他称这是未来研究的一个“开创性机会”。

sentences.en: But he added that additional study is needed to confirm the team’s latest findings.
sentences.zh: 但他补充说，还需要进一步研究来证实该团队的最新发现。

sentences.en: "As exciting as the new findings are, we realize that our results can only be verified by samples from Mars, which are currently being collected by NASA's Perseverance rover,” Mustard said.
sentences.zh: “这些新发现固然令人兴奋，但我们意识到，我们的结果只能通过火星样本加以验证，而NASA的‘毅力号’漫游车目前正在采集这些样本，”马斯特说。

sentences.en: He added, “When we get those back, we will be able to check whether our theory about ferrihydrite is correct."
sentences.zh: 他补充道：‘等我们把这些样本带回来后，就能检验我们关于铁水铝石的理论是否正确。’

sentences.en: I’m Bryan Lynn.
sentences.zh: 我是布莱恩·林恩。

glossary.def: new or different from anything else
a situation in which it is possible for someone to do something
to confirm whether something is true
to find out if something is correct or not
